categories.name: AI Tools
categories.description: Assistants, copilots and local models that use machine learning to help you work.

categories.name: AI Assistants
categories.description: Conversational AI assistants for writing, research, analysis and everyday questions.

categories.name: AI Coding Tools
categories.description: Code completion, chat and agents that help developers write and understand code.

categories.name: Productivity
categories.description: Tools for notes, tasks, documents and getting organised.

categories.name: Note Taking
categories.description: Apps for capturing notes, building a knowledge base and linking ideas.
categories.seoIntro: Note-taking apps range from cloud workspaces built for teams to local-first Markdown editors that keep your files on your own device. Compare them by where your data lives, whether they work offline, how they sync and whether they support linking notes together.

categories.name: Project Management
categories.description: Plan, track and ship work with boards, timelines and tasks.

categories.name: Office Suites
categories.description: Word processors, spreadsheets and presentation software.

categories.name: PDF Tools
categories.description: View, annotate, edit, merge and convert PDF documents.

categories.name: Automation
categories.description: Connect apps and automate repetitive workflows.

categories.name: Design
categories.description: Graphic design, photo and video creation tools.

categories.name: Graphic Design
categories.description: Vector, UI and illustration tools for designers.

categories.name: Photo Editing
categories.description: Raster image editors and RAW photo developers.
categories.seoIntro: Photo editors split into layer-based raster editors for retouching and compositing, and RAW developers built around a non-destructive photography workflow. Free open-source options cover most needs; paid suites add AI tools and ecosystem integration.

categories.name: Video Editing
categories.description: Non-linear editors for cutting, grading and finishing video.
categories.seoIntro: Video editors differ in timeline depth, colour tools, performance and price. Several professional-grade editors are free, while subscription suites focus on ecosystem integration.

categories.name: Developer Tools
categories.description: Editors, databases and tools for building software.

categories.name: Code Editors
categories.description: Text editors and IDEs for writing code.

categories.name: Databases
categories.description: Database engines and database management tools.

categories.name: Security & Privacy
categories.description: Protect accounts, data and browsing.

categories.name: Password Managers
categories.description: Store, generate and autofill passwords securely.
categories.seoIntro: A password manager generates strong, unique passwords and fills them in for you. The main differences are whether the vault lives in the cloud or only on your device, whether the code is open source, and which platforms and browsers are supported.

categories.name: Internet
categories.description: Browsers and cloud storage.

categories.name: Web Browsers
categories.description: Browsers for desktop and mobile.
categories.seoIntro: Most browsers today use either Chromium or Mozilla's Gecko engine. Compare them on privacy defaults, built-in blocking, sync and extension support.

categories.name: Cloud Storage
categories.description: Sync, store and share files across devices.

categories.name: Business
categories.description: CRM and analytics for running a business.

categories.name: CRM
categories.description: Customer relationship management: contacts, deals and pipelines.

categories.name: Web Analytics
categories.description: Measure website traffic and user behaviour.
categories.seoIntro: Web analytics tools measure visits and conversions. Privacy-focused tools avoid cookies and personal data, which can simplify consent requirements, while larger platforms offer deeper advertising integration.

categories.name: Marketing
categories.description: Email marketing and website building.

categories.name: Email Marketing
categories.description: Newsletters, campaigns and email automation.

categories.name: Website Builders
categories.description: Build and publish websites and blogs.

categories.name: Communication
categories.description: Team chat, messaging and calls.

applications.name: ChatGPT
applications.shortDescription: OpenAI's conversational AI assistant for writing, analysis, coding help and research.
applications.description: ChatGPT is a chat-based assistant built on OpenAI's language models. It can draft and edit text, answer questions, analyse uploaded files and search the web, with a free tier and paid plans.

applications.name: Claude
applications.shortDescription: Anthropic's AI assistant for writing, analysis, coding and long documents.
applications.description: Claude is an AI assistant developed by Anthropic. It handles long documents and files, helps with writing and code, and offers a free tier alongside paid plans.

applications.name: Google Gemini
applications.shortDescription: Google's AI assistant, integrated with Google search and Workspace.
applications.description: Gemini is Google's conversational AI assistant. It can search the web, work with uploaded files and connects to Google services, with free and paid tiers.

applications.name: Perplexity
applications.shortDescription: An AI answer engine that searches the web and cites its sources.
applications.description: Perplexity combines a language model with live web search and shows the sources behind each answer. A free tier is available with a paid Pro plan.

applications.name: LM Studio
applications.shortDescription: Desktop app for downloading and running open large language models locally.
applications.description: LM Studio lets you discover, download and chat with open-weight language models entirely on your own computer, and can expose them through a local API server.

applications.name: Ollama
applications.shortDescription: Run open large language models locally from the command line or a local API.
applications.description: Ollama is an open-source tool for running open-weight language models on your own machine. It provides a CLI and a local HTTP API and can run in Docker.

applications.name: GitHub Copilot
applications.shortDescription: AI pair programmer that suggests code and answers questions inside your editor.
applications.description: GitHub Copilot provides inline code completions, chat and agent features in editors such as VS Code, Visual Studio and JetBrains IDEs. It has a free tier and paid plans.

applications.name: Cursor
applications.shortDescription: An AI-first code editor built on the VS Code foundation.
applications.description: Cursor is a code editor with AI completion, chat and multi-file editing built in. It supports VS Code extensions and offers a free tier with paid plans.

applications.name: Continue
applications.shortDescription: Open-source AI code assistant extension for VS Code and JetBrains.
applications.description: Continue is an open-source extension that adds chat, autocomplete and editing powered by the model of your choice, including local models, to VS Code and JetBrains IDEs.

applications.name: Notion
applications.shortDescription: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, wikis and lightweight databases.
applications.description: Notion combines pages, wikis, task boards and relational databases in one collaborative workspace. Teams use it for documentation and planning; a free plan is available.

applications.name: Obsidian
applications.shortDescription: Local-first Markdown knowledge base with backlinks and a large plugin ecosystem.
applications.description: Obsidian stores notes as plain Markdown files on your device and links them together with backlinks and a graph view. The app is free; sync and publishing are paid add-ons.

applications.name: Joplin
applications.shortDescription: Open-source note-taking app with Markdown and end-to-end encrypted sync.
applications.description: Joplin organises notes into notebooks using Markdown and can sync through Joplin Cloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, WebDAV or a self-hosted Joplin Server, with optional end-to-end encryption.

applications.name: Logseq
applications.shortDescription: Open-source outliner for networked notes and journals stored as local files.
applications.description: Logseq is a privacy-first outliner where every block can be linked and referenced. Notes are stored locally as Markdown or Org files and visualised in a graph.

applications.name: Evernote
applications.shortDescription: Long-running note-taking app with web clipping, notebooks and search.
applications.description: Evernote captures notes, web clippings, documents and images into searchable notebooks synced across devices, with a limited free plan and paid tiers.

applications.name: Standard Notes
applications.shortDescription: End-to-end encrypted notes app focused on privacy and longevity.
applications.description: Standard Notes encrypts every note end-to-end and syncs across devices. The server can be self-hosted, and paid plans unlock extra editors and storage.

applications.name: AppFlowy
applications.shortDescription: Open-source, self-hostable workspace for docs, wikis and databases.
applications.description: AppFlowy offers Notion-style documents, boards and grid databases. It is open source, works offline and can be self-hosted, with an optional paid cloud.

applications.name: Trello
applications.shortDescription: Visual Kanban boards for organising tasks and projects.
applications.description: Trello organises work into boards, lists and cards that teams move through stages. Power-Ups add integrations; a free plan is available.

applications.name: Asana
applications.shortDescription: Work management platform for tasks, projects, timelines and portfolios.
applications.description: Asana helps teams plan projects with lists, boards, timelines and goals, and automate routine work with rules. A free plan covers small teams.

applications.name: ClickUp
applications.shortDescription: All-in-one productivity platform with tasks, docs, goals and whiteboards.
applications.description: ClickUp combines task management with docs, chat, whiteboards and dashboards and offers many views including list, board and Gantt. A free plan is available.

applications.name: Plane
applications.shortDescription: Open-source project tracking for issues, cycles and roadmaps.
applications.description: Plane is an open-source alternative to tools like Jira and Linear with issues, cycles, modules and multiple layouts. It can be self-hosted with Docker or used in the cloud.

applications.name: OpenProject
applications.shortDescription: Open-source project management with Gantt charts, work packages and agile boards.
applications.description: OpenProject supports classic, agile and hybrid project management, including Gantt charts, time tracking and boards. The Community edition is free to self-host.

applications.name: Figma
applications.shortDescription: Collaborative interface design and prototyping tool in the browser.
applications.description: Figma is a vector design tool for UI and product design with real-time multiplayer editing, prototyping and a plugin ecosystem. It runs in the browser and as a desktop app.

applications.name: Penpot
applications.shortDescription: Open-source design and prototyping platform built on open web standards.
applications.description: Penpot is a browser-based design and prototyping tool that uses SVG as its native format. Teams can use the hosted service or self-host it with Docker.

applications.name: Inkscape
applications.shortDescription: Free and open-source vector graphics editor for illustration and SVG.
applications.description: Inkscape is a professional vector graphics editor that uses SVG as its native format, suited to illustrations, diagrams, logos and print layouts.

applications.name: Canva
applications.shortDescription: Online design platform with templates for social posts, presentations and print.
applications.description: Canva provides drag-and-drop design with a large template library for social media, presentations, documents and marketing materials. A free plan is available.

applications.name: Sketch
applications.shortDescription: Native macOS design tool for interfaces, icons and prototypes.
applications.description: Sketch is a vector design app for macOS focused on UI and icon design, with symbols, prototyping, a web app for collaboration and a plugin ecosystem.

applications.name: Krita
applications.shortDescription: Free and open-source digital painting application.
applications.description: Krita is a painting program made by artists for concept art, illustration, comics and textures, with brush engines, layers and animation tools.

applications.name: Adobe Photoshop
applications.shortDescription: Industry-standard raster image editor for photography and design.
applications.description: Photoshop is Adobe's image editor for retouching, compositing and graphic design, with layers, masks, Camera Raw and generative tools. It is sold by subscription.

applications.name: GIMP
applications.shortDescription: Free and open-source raster image editor.
applications.description: GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program) is a cross-platform image editor for retouching, composition and authoring, extensible with plugins and scripts.

applications.name: Photopea
applications.shortDescription: Browser-based image editor that opens PSD, XCF and Sketch files.
applications.description: Photopea is an online image editor with a Photoshop-like interface. It runs entirely in the browser, supports layered PSD files and is free with ads or ad-free with a premium account.

applications.name: darktable
applications.shortDescription: Open-source RAW photo developer and photography workflow app.
applications.description: darktable manages digital negatives in a database and lets you develop RAW photos with a non-destructive editing pipeline.

applications.name: DaVinci Resolve
applications.shortDescription: Professional editing, color grading, VFX and audio post-production in one app.
applications.description: DaVinci Resolve by Blackmagic Design combines editing, colour correction, visual effects and audio post-production. A capable free version is available; Resolve Studio is a one-time purchase.

applications.name: Adobe Premiere Pro
applications.shortDescription: Professional non-linear video editor by Adobe.
applications.description: Premiere Pro is Adobe's timeline-based video editor used in film, TV and online video, integrated with After Effects and other Creative Cloud apps.

applications.name: Kdenlive
applications.shortDescription: Open-source non-linear video editor from the KDE community.
applications.description: Kdenlive is a multi-track video editor supporting many formats, effects, transitions and proxy editing.

applications.name: Shotcut
applications.shortDescription: Free, open-source, cross-platform video editor.
applications.description: Shotcut is a video editor built on the MLT framework with wide format support, native timeline editing and a range of filters.

applications.name: OpenShot
applications.shortDescription: Simple open-source video editor for beginners.
applications.description: OpenShot is an easy-to-use video editor with drag-and-drop, unlimited tracks, transitions and title templates.

applications.name: CapCut
applications.shortDescription: Template-driven video editor for short-form social video.
applications.description: CapCut is a video editor from ByteDance aimed at social video, with templates, auto captions and effects across mobile, desktop and web. Core features are free with a paid Pro plan.

applications.name: Bitwarden
applications.shortDescription: Open-source password manager with end-to-end encryption and self-hosting.
applications.description: Bitwarden stores passwords, passkeys and notes in an end-to-end encrypted vault available on every major platform. The free plan includes unlimited devices; the server can be self-hosted.

applications.name: 1Password
applications.shortDescription: Password manager for individuals, families and businesses.
applications.description: 1Password keeps passwords, passkeys and sensitive documents in an end-to-end encrypted vault with autofill on desktop, mobile and the browser. It is subscription-based with a free trial.

applications.name: KeePassXC
applications.shortDescription: Offline, open-source password manager storing an encrypted local database.
applications.description: KeePassXC is a community fork of KeePassX that keeps passwords in an encrypted KDBX file on your device. It works offline, integrates with browsers and can generate TOTP codes.

applications.name: Proton Pass
applications.shortDescription: End-to-end encrypted password manager from the makers of Proton Mail.
applications.description: Proton Pass stores logins, passkeys and notes with end-to-end encryption and offers hide-my-email aliases. Apps are open source; a free plan is available.

applications.name: Mozilla Firefox
applications.shortDescription: Independent open-source web browser with built-in tracking protection.
applications.description: Firefox is developed by Mozilla on its own Gecko engine. It includes Enhanced Tracking Protection, sync across devices and a large add-on catalogue.

applications.name: Google Chrome
applications.shortDescription: Google's Chromium-based web browser.
applications.description: Chrome is Google's web browser built on the open-source Chromium project, with sync through a Google account and the Chrome Web Store for extensions.

applications.name: Brave
applications.shortDescription: Chromium-based browser that blocks ads and trackers by default.
applications.description: Brave is an open-source browser built on Chromium with built-in ad and tracker blocking (Brave Shields) and support for Chrome extensions.

applications.name: Vivaldi
applications.shortDescription: Highly customisable browser with built-in tools like mail, calendar and tab stacking.
applications.description: Vivaldi is a Chromium-based browser focused on customisation, with tab stacking, a built-in ad and tracker blocker, mail client and notes.

applications.name: Visual Studio Code
applications.shortDescription: Free code editor from Microsoft with a huge extension marketplace.
applications.description: Visual Studio Code is a lightweight, extensible source-code editor with debugging, Git integration, IntelliSense and thousands of extensions. It runs on desktop and in the browser.

applications.name: VSCodium
applications.shortDescription: Community-built, telemetry-free binaries of the open-source VS Code project.
applications.description: VSCodium distributes builds of Microsoft's MIT-licensed VS Code source without Microsoft branding and telemetry, using the Open VSX extension registry.

applications.name: Sublime Text
applications.shortDescription: Fast, sophisticated text editor for code and prose.
applications.description: Sublime Text is a cross-platform text editor known for speed, multiple selections and a command palette. It can be evaluated for free and requires a one-time licence for continued use.

applications.name: PostgreSQL
applications.shortDescription: Powerful open-source object-relational database system.
applications.description: PostgreSQL is an advanced open-source relational database with strong standards compliance, extensibility, JSON support and a large extension ecosystem.

applications.name: MySQL
applications.shortDescription: Widely used open-source relational database by Oracle.
applications.description: MySQL is a popular relational database available as a free Community Edition under the GPL and commercial editions from Oracle.

applications.name: MongoDB
applications.shortDescription: Document database storing data as flexible JSON-like documents.
applications.description: MongoDB is a document-oriented database. The Community Server is free under the SSPL, and MongoDB Atlas is a managed cloud service with a free tier.

applications.name: SQLite
applications.shortDescription: Small, fast, self-contained, embedded SQL database engine.
applications.description: SQLite is a serverless SQL database engine stored in a single file. It is in the public domain and embedded in countless applications and devices.

applications.name: DBeaver
applications.shortDescription: Universal database client for SQL and NoSQL databases.
applications.description: DBeaver is a cross-platform database tool supporting many databases via JDBC. The Community edition is open source; commercial editions add NoSQL and cloud features.

applications.name: Slack
applications.shortDescription: Team messaging organised into channels with integrations and huddles.
applications.description: Slack brings team conversations into channels and threads, with file sharing, audio and video huddles and thousands of integrations. A limited free plan is available.

applications.name: Discord
applications.shortDescription: Voice, video and text chat for communities and friends.
applications.description: Discord organises communities into servers with text channels, voice channels and video calls. It is free to use, with an optional Nitro subscription.

applications.name: Microsoft Teams
applications.shortDescription: Chat, meetings and collaboration in Microsoft 365.
applications.description: Microsoft Teams combines chat, video meetings, file collaboration and integrations with Microsoft 365 apps. A free version is available for personal use.

applications.name: Mattermost
applications.shortDescription: Open-source, self-hostable team messaging and collaboration platform.
applications.description: Mattermost provides channel-based messaging, playbooks and integrations that organisations can self-host for control over their data.

applications.name: Element
applications.shortDescription: Secure messaging and collaboration built on the open Matrix protocol.
applications.description: Element is a Matrix client offering end-to-end encrypted chat, voice and video. Users can join any Matrix homeserver or host their own.

applications.name: Signal
applications.shortDescription: Private messenger with end-to-end encryption for messages and calls.
applications.description: Signal is a non-profit, open-source messaging app using the Signal Protocol to end-to-end encrypt messages, voice and video calls by default.

applications.name: Dropbox
applications.shortDescription: Cloud storage and file sync for individuals and teams.
applications.description: Dropbox syncs files across devices, shares folders and links, and keeps version history. A small free plan is available with paid tiers for more storage.

applications.name: Google Drive
applications.shortDescription: Cloud storage integrated with Google Docs, Sheets and Slides.
applications.description: Google Drive stores and syncs files and is the home for Google Docs, Sheets and Slides with real-time collaboration. Free storage is shared across Google services.

applications.name: Nextcloud
applications.shortDescription: Self-hosted content collaboration platform for files, calendars and more.
applications.description: Nextcloud lets organisations run their own file sync and share service with calendars, contacts, office editing and many apps, on their own servers.

applications.name: Proton Drive
applications.shortDescription: End-to-end encrypted cloud storage from Proton.
applications.description: Proton Drive encrypts files end-to-end before they leave your device and syncs them across platforms. A free plan with limited storage is available.

applications.name: Syncthing
applications.shortDescription: Open-source continuous file synchronisation between your own devices.
applications.description: Syncthing syncs folders directly between devices over encrypted connections without a central cloud server.

applications.name: Zapier
applications.shortDescription: No-code automation connecting thousands of web apps.
applications.description: Zapier connects web apps through triggers and actions so routine tasks run automatically. A free plan covers simple automations.

applications.name: Make
applications.shortDescription: Visual automation platform for building multi-step scenarios.
applications.description: Make (formerly Integromat) lets you design automation scenarios on a visual canvas with branching, iterators and error handling. A free plan is available.

applications.name: n8n
applications.shortDescription: Fair-code workflow automation you can self-host.
applications.description: n8n is a node-based workflow automation tool that can be self-hosted or used in the cloud. Its source is available under the Sustainable Use License.

applications.name: Node-RED
applications.shortDescription: Open-source flow-based programming tool for wiring together devices and APIs.
applications.description: Node-RED provides a browser-based editor to wire together flows from a palette of nodes. It runs on Node.js, including on low-cost hardware.

applications.name: Google Analytics
applications.shortDescription: Google's web and app analytics service.
applications.description: Google Analytics measures website and app traffic with event-based tracking, reports and audiences. The standard product is free; Analytics 360 is a paid enterprise tier.

applications.name: Plausible Analytics
applications.shortDescription: Lightweight, privacy-friendly website analytics without cookies.
applications.description: Plausible is an open-source web analytics tool that does not use cookies and collects no personal data. It is offered as a paid cloud service or a self-hosted Community Edition.

applications.name: Matomo
applications.shortDescription: Open-source analytics platform that gives you full data ownership.
applications.description: Matomo (formerly Piwik) is a web analytics platform you can self-host for free or use in Matomo Cloud, with heatmaps and other premium plugins available.

applications.name: Umami
applications.shortDescription: Simple, open-source, privacy-focused website analytics.
applications.description: Umami is a lightweight analytics tool that does not use cookies. It can be self-hosted for free or used through Umami Cloud.

applications.name: HubSpot CRM
applications.shortDescription: Free CRM with marketing, sales and service hubs on top.
applications.description: HubSpot CRM tracks contacts, companies and deals for free, with paid Marketing, Sales and Service Hubs adding automation and reporting.

applications.name: Salesforce Sales Cloud
applications.shortDescription: Enterprise CRM for sales teams.
applications.description: Salesforce Sales Cloud manages leads, opportunities and forecasts with extensive customisation and a large app marketplace. It is sold by subscription with a free trial.

applications.name: Twenty
applications.shortDescription: Open-source CRM with a modern interface, self-hostable or in the cloud.
applications.description: Twenty is an open-source CRM for managing companies, people and opportunities with customisable objects and an API. It can be self-hosted with Docker.

applications.name: SuiteCRM
applications.shortDescription: Open-source CRM originally forked from SugarCRM.
applications.description: SuiteCRM is a self-hosted open-source CRM covering sales, marketing and customer service, with workflows and reporting.

applications.name: Mailchimp
applications.shortDescription: Email marketing and automation platform for small businesses.
applications.description: Mailchimp provides email campaigns, audience management, templates and marketing automation, with a limited free plan.

applications.name: listmonk
applications.shortDescription: Self-hosted, high-performance newsletter and mailing list manager.
applications.description: listmonk is an open-source, single-binary newsletter and mailing list manager with templates, analytics and an API.

applications.name: WordPress
applications.shortDescription: Open-source CMS powering a large share of the web.
applications.description: WordPress is a free, open-source content management system for blogs and websites, extended with themes and plugins. It can be self-hosted or used via managed hosts.

applications.name: Ghost
applications.shortDescription: Open-source publishing platform for blogs, newsletters and memberships.
applications.description: Ghost is a Node.js publishing platform with built-in newsletters and paid memberships. It can be self-hosted for free or run on Ghost(Pro).

applications.name: Wix
applications.shortDescription: Drag-and-drop website builder with hosting included.
applications.description: Wix lets you build websites from templates with a visual editor, and adds blogging, booking and online store features. A free plan shows Wix branding.

applications.name: Webflow
applications.shortDescription: Visual web design platform that produces clean, production-ready sites.
applications.description: Webflow combines a visual designer with a CMS and hosting, aimed at designers who want control over layout and interactions without hand-coding.

applications.name: LibreOffice
applications.shortDescription: Free and open-source office suite.
applications.description: LibreOffice includes Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw and Base, works offline and uses the OpenDocument format while opening Microsoft Office files.

applications.name: Microsoft 365
applications.shortDescription: Microsoft's Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook with cloud services.
applications.description: Microsoft 365 bundles the Office apps with OneDrive storage and collaboration. Web versions are free with a Microsoft account; desktop apps need a subscription.

applications.name: Google Docs
applications.shortDescription: Browser-based word processor with real-time collaboration.
applications.description: Google Docs, along with Sheets and Slides, lets people write and edit documents together in real time in the browser, free with a Google account.

applications.name: ONLYOFFICE
applications.shortDescription: Open-source office suite with collaborative editing, desktop and self-hosted.
applications.description: ONLYOFFICE offers document, spreadsheet and presentation editors with strong Microsoft Office format compatibility. Docs can be self-hosted and integrated with platforms like Nextcloud.

applications.name: Adobe Acrobat
applications.shortDescription: Adobe's PDF viewer and editor.
applications.description: Adobe Acrobat Reader is a free PDF viewer with annotation and form filling; Acrobat Pro adds editing, conversion and e-signature features by subscription.

applications.name: Okular
applications.shortDescription: KDE's universal document viewer with PDF annotation.
applications.description: Okular views PDF, EPUB, comics and many other formats, with annotations, form filling and digital signature support.

applications.name: Stirling-PDF
applications.shortDescription: Self-hosted web app for merging, splitting, converting and editing PDFs.
applications.description: Stirling-PDF runs locally or on your server via Docker and offers dozens of PDF operations without sending documents to third-party services.
